Drag and drop the blocks below to create a proof by induction of the following statement.

Claim: for all natural numbers $n$,
\(\sum_{j=0}^n 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{n+1}}{4}\)

blocks.text: Base case: At $n=0$, $\sum_{j=0}^n 2(-7)^j = 2$ and $\frac{1-(-7)^{n+1}}{4} = \frac{1-(-7)}{4} = 2$, so the base case $P(0)$ holds.
Base case: At $n=0$, $\sum_{j=0}^n 2(-7)^j = 2$. So the base case $P(0)$ holds.
Inductive Hypothesis: Suppose that $P(n):$ $\sum_{j=0}^n 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{n+1}}{4}$ holds for $n=0,1,…,k$.
Inductive Step: We need to show that $P(k+1):$ $\sum_{j=0}^{k+1} 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{k+2}}{4}$ holds.
Inductive Step: We need to show that $P(k+1):$ $\sum_{j=0}^{k} 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{k+2}}{4}$ holds.
The left hand side is $\sum_{j=0}^{k+1} 2(-7)^j = \sum_{j=0}^k 2(-7)^j + 2(-7)^{k+1}$”> The left hand side is $\sum_{j=0}^{k+1} 2(-7)^j = \sum_{j=0}^k 2(-7)^j + 2(-7)^{k+1}$.

By the inductive hypothesis we have $\sum_{j=0}^k 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{k+1}}{4}$. So then substituting we get $\frac{1-(-7)^{k+1}}{4} + 2(-7)^{k+1}$ $= \frac{1-(-7)^{k+1} + 8(-7)^{k+1}}{4}$ $= \frac{1+7(-7)^{k+1}}{4}$ which simplifies to $= \frac{1-(-7)^{k+2}}{4}$

By the inductive hypothesis we have $\sum_{j=0}^{k+1} 2(-7)^j = \sum_{j=0}^k 2(-7)^j + 2(-7)^{k+1}$. So then substituting we get $\frac{1-(-7)^{k+1}}{4} + 2(-7)^{k+1}$ $= \frac{1-(-7)^{k+1} + 8(-7)^{k+1}}{4}$ $= \frac{1+7(-7)^{k+1}}{4}$ which simplifies to $= \frac{1-(-7)^{k+2}}{4}$
So $\sum_{j=0}^{k+1} 2(-7)^j = \frac{1-(-7)^{k+2}}{4}$, which was what we needed to show.
